findings.finding: Root spec's 'names this issue' is read as the child key LEGSMOKE-983, yet every existing smoke/LEGSMOKE-*.md (973, 974 cited) is root-keyed; no file in smoke/ is named after a child.

findings.finding: For a reviewer-given K=1 text the implementer both set and reported the expected bytes, leaving the tester nothing independent to check against.
findings.answer: Decision 5: the reviewer writes the exact line as a fenced literal in its REQUEST_CHANGES review; the tester computes size and sha itself from that literal with printf | git hash-object --stdin, never from the implementer's numbers; the default text's bytes (85, bd297bf7...) are pre-computed.

findings.finding: The child spec is empty and the root spec has no Acceptance section, so LIT, the path and C1-C6 are planner-derived and approved by no one.
findings.answer: Stated in plan.md 'Spec this plan builds': the derivation is the plan's; the child spec and its sign-off are the architect's; the literal goes to the architect in the completion summary, who may overrule it before the implementer's targeted message (the implementer re-reads the plan at start); the planner edits no spec.

findings.finding: 'Nothing else changes' versus the mid-run .legion/LEGSMOKE-983/*.json commits; no stated fallback if retro leaves them.
findings.answer: Decision 4: handoffs are artifacts the legion-worker completion gate requires; the scope sentence is judged on the merged result M (C5); mid-run they are excluded (C2a) and retro removes them (C2b); a head offered for READY still carrying .legion/ gets no READY, the merger reports to the architect, who re-runs retro (the implementer); the reviewer removes nothing.

findings.finding: C5 depends on a squash merge no role may perform, so the final criterion is reachable only through an actor the plan did not name.
findings.answer: Decision 13: the daemon submits the merge on READY's acceptance (legion-worker 'the merge gate'; PR #734 merged as 841a4227 that way); if M has not landed when the production-check task arrives, the implementer reports the PR state to the architect and holds; C5 is never waived.

findings.finding: C4 allowed 'if the approval is voided, re-approve' and C3's negative control was 'read, not provoked', so neither decided itself.
findings.answer: C4 requires reviewDecision APPROVED at R unconditionally; the normal path is the approval of A persisting (ruleset 24471196 has no dismiss-stale rule; PR #734: approval at 7fb21d30, retro 200d1dae after it, still APPROVED); otherwise the reviewer re-approves R before READY. C3's negative control is the real failing run 39526057184 (fail-on-demand, failure, head beb7bfb1), re-read by the tester with gh run view.

findings.finding: C1 derived H from jj log -r @-, which after the implementer's handoff commit names the handoff commit, so the tester's 'verbatim' re-run would record a different H.
findings.answer: Decision 12: the implementer records H once (right after the code split, before the handoff split) as headSha in every implement.json proof entry and the E2E line; tester and reviewer read H=$(jq -r '.proof[0].headSha' .legion/LEGSMOKE-983/implement.json); C1 uses that H.

findings.answer: Measurements: .codegraph/ has 0 tracked paths on main and jj status is clean (jj snapshots nothing there); decision 3 names a .codegraph/ file, a stray /tmp copy and .fail-me as rows that make 'jj diff -r @- --summary' != 'A smoke/LEGSMOKE-983.md' a failed scope to fix before pushing.
